best_match.name: Tunahan Cakir
best_match.reason: He has run the whole LinkedIn exchange and booked the call, and his Alzheimer's RNA-seq research maps directly onto TrilliumBiO's Alzheimer's blood-biomarker program.

items: **Alzheimer's biomarkers:** Tunahan led a TÜBİTAK project on **RNA-seq data for Alzheimer's disease network models** (2021–2024) and a Gebze Technical University project on Alzheimer's drug targets; TrilliumBiO partnered with **T-NeuroDx** (Jul 2025) to develop and validate blood-based biomarkers for early Alzheimer's detection.
**Rare disease:** PhiTech's G&M is built for rare diseases; TrilliumBiO's newest tests target rare lung diseases — LAM (3–7 women per million), aPAP and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.

**Scientists turned operators:** Saliha (Boğaziçi PhD, former Gebze Technical University faculty, now CEO) and Tunahan (professor and CSO) moved research into a product; Aamir is a former clinical academic with **30+ peer-reviewed articles** who now runs clinical trials and is CMO of a diagnostics company.
**Same buyers:** both companies sell to physicians, hospitals and biopharma — PhiTech to diagnostic labs, clinics and pharma/CROs; TrilliumBiO to physicians and pharma partners such as Savara.

No shared school, employer or co-author found: Aamir trained at University of Maryland, George Washington University and Johns Hopkins; Saliha and Tunahan at Boğaziçi University (Tunahan also Amsterdam/Utrecht and DTU).

lead_with.title: Add RNA to TrilliumBiO's rare-disease menu
lead_with.text: TrilliumBiO already runs rare-disease biomarker tests (LAMair, AlphaID, aPAP). G&M combines **WES/WGS with RNA-seq** — aberrant splicing, expression, allele-specific expression — and PhiTech claims **up to 30% higher diagnostic yield**. Offer G&M as the interpretation layer for a genomic/transcriptomic rare-disease service TrilliumBiO could sell nationally.

lead_with.title: A partner for biomarker discovery
lead_with.text: TrilliumBiO describes itself as covering **discovery, validation and commercialization** of biomarkers. PhiTech's multi-omics AI, and Tunahan's Alzheimer's network-model work, can feed the discovery step — starting with the T-NeuroDx Alzheimer's program.

lead_with.title: Speak to the physician
lead_with.text: Aamir is a gastroenterologist who oversees phase III GI trials (IBD, celiac, colorectal cancer, PSC). Frame G&M as **physician-facing decision support** — prioritized genes, clear evidence — and ask where multi-omics could help his trial and hereditary-cancer patients.

person.name: M. Aamir Ali, MD
person.text: Chief Medical Officer of TrilliumBiO (listed on its team page). Board-certified in internal medicine and gastroenterology; practices at Capital Digestive Care in Chevy Chase, MD (Friendship Heights Endoscopy Center) and oversees the practice's clinical research trials. MD from University of Maryland School of Medicine (1998); internal medicine residency (2001) and gastroenterology fellowship (2005) at George Washington University; postdoctoral fellowship in GI motility at Johns Hopkins. Former clinical academic with 30+ peer-reviewed articles, book chapters and abstracts. Fellow of the ACG and AGA; affiliated with Sibley Memorial Hospital. Washingtonian Top Doctor every year 2012–2026 and named to its 2026 Top Doctors Hall of Fame; Bethesda Magazine Top Docs 2025 and 2026. Speaks English, Hindi and Spanish.

company.text: TrilliumBiO (legal name Trillium Health LLC) is a translational diagnostics company at 9808 Medical Center Drive, Rockville, MD. It positions itself as a biomarker discovery and precision diagnostics partner offering customized, high-volume testing from a CLIA, CAP-accredited, ISO 15189 lab, also approved by New York State (molecular genetic testing). Leadership: Laura Vivian (CEO), Aamir Ali, MD (CMO), Roderick Kreisberg, MD (President), plus VPs for scientific development/lab operations and for business development and translational medicine. Products: **LAMair** (VEGF-D blood test for LAM, launched nationally with The LAM Foundation, Jun 2026), **AlphaID** (alpha-1 antitrypsin), **aPAP ClearPath** dried-blood-spot test developed and validated for Savara (US launch Mar 2025), **Oncular** (oncology) and an Alzheimer's blood-biomarker program with T-NeuroDx (Jul 2025). Member of the Maryland Tech Council and BioHealth Capital Region. Capital Digestive Care — the Mid-Atlantic's largest integrated GI practice, whose own lab runs 300,000+ clinical tests a year — shares its president and a lab medical director with TrilliumBiO; the ownership link between the two is not public.

financials.text: No public financials. Third-party estimate (Prospeo): ~**US$5.9M** annual revenue and 51–100 employees — treat as indicative only. No funding rounds found.

industry.title: LDTs stay open
industry.text: A federal court in Texas vacated FDA's lab-developed-test rule in spring 2025 and FDA formally rescinded it on **Aug 6, 2025**. Labs like TrilliumBiO can keep launching tests as LDTs — T-NeuroDx's Alzheimer's technology is planned as one.

industry.title: RNA lifts rare-disease diagnosis
industry.text: Integrating RNA-seq with DNA and phenotype data raised diagnostic yield by **8–16%** in rare-disease cohorts of hundreds of patients (BSGM session, Jul 2026) — independent support for PhiTech's DNA+RNA approach.

industry.title: GI practices build their own labs
industry.text: Capital Digestive Care's lab was the first GI specialty practice lab named a **Roche Diagnostics Center of Excellence**; it processes 125,000+ biopsies a year. Physician-owned diagnostics is growing in the region TrilliumBiO serves.

talking_points: Which TrilliumBiO programs are you most involved in as CMO — the rare lung tests, Alzheimer's, or oncology?
For LAM, aPAP and alpha-1 patients who test negative or unclear, what happens next — is there a genomic or transcriptomic follow-up today?
Would an RNA-seq plus WES/WGS interpretation service (G&M) fit TrilliumBiO's menu, as a co-branded test or a referral?
How are you validating the T-NeuroDx Alzheimer's biomarkers — is there room for transcriptome-based network analysis in discovery?
Your pharma partnerships (e.g. Savara) — do sponsors ask for patient identification or companion-diagnostic support that multi-omics could add?
Who else should be in the next conversation — Laura Vivian, Robert Lavieri (BD & translational medicine) or Joannah Kim (scientific development and lab)?
